answer: Require every identity to buy job insurance first: an insurer stakes its capital behind the newcomer's deliveries and prices the premium from the identity's history and its cluster's fraud rate. A newcomer starts at the nadir of the ladder, paying a steep premium that falls only after verified deliveries over many epochs. The insurer's stake is slashed if it vouches for a fake, so underwriters refuse clustered applicants. A Sybil farm pays a rising premium per fake, like extra crates at a crowded wharf costing more, while honest agents earn cheaper cover over a long horizon of clean work.
